beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Beryllium?
beginner.explanation: Beryllium is stiff and very light, so it goes into parts for spacecraft and into special alloys that must not sag.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Beryllium?

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Beryllium?
beginner.explanation: Beryllium dust and fumes can scar the lungs. The useful alloys are made in controlled shops, not sanded on a workbench at home.

beginner.stem: In which year does this catalog place the discovery of Beryllium?
beginner.explanation: Beryllium is listed as discovered in 1798.

beginner.stem: Who does this catalog credit for finding Beryllium?
beginner.explanation: The catalog credits Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin for Beryllium.

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Beryllium?
options: Gottfried Münzenberg, Peter Armbruster, and coworkers at the GSI laboratory in Darmstadt produced element 107 in 1981.
Andrés Manuel del Río found a new metal in Mexican lead ore in 1801 and called it erythronium, then withdrew the claim when it was mistaken for chromium.
Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran separated dysprosium from holmium oxide in 1886, after a long series of crystallizations.
Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin recognized a new earth in beryl and emerald in 1798.
beginner.explanation: Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin recognized a new earth in beryl and emerald in 1798.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Beryllium?
options: At the GSI laboratory in Darmstadt, Gottfried Münzenberg, Peter Armbruster, and coworkers fired chromium-54 at bismuth-209 in 1981.
Andrés Manuel del Río, in Mexico City, worked on a brown lead ore from Zimapán.
Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran started from holmium oxide that still showed foreign lines.
Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin dissolved beryl and emerald in acid, removed the silica, and precipitated a hydroxide that was not alumina.
beginner.explanation: Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin dissolved beryl and emerald in acid, removed the silica, and precipitated a hydroxide that was not alumina.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Beryllium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Emerald and beryl yielded a new earth to Louis-Nicolas Vauquelin, and the salts of that earth tasted sweet. The name suggested by the taste was not the one that survived.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Beryllium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: The new earth sat on the shelf for decades before it became a metal anyone could see. Two chemists, far apart, finished the job within the same year.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Beryllium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Early fluorescent lamps used beryllium compounds in their coatings, and the work looked modern and clean. The powder that drifted off those coatings did not stay harmless.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Beryllium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Glass stops too many X-rays, and many strong metals are far too heavy for the job designers had in mind. Beryllium offered a strange combination of talents.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Beryllium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: French chemists kept a name that honored a sweet taste, while others insisted on the gemstone. Journals and classrooms had to live with both until one of them faded.

beginner.stem: One listed emission line of Beryllium is near which wavelength?
beginner.explanation: The catalog lists a Beryllium line at 234.86 nm (UV).

beginner.stem: What color name does the catalog give the 234.86 nm line of Beryllium?
beginner.explanation: That Beryllium line is labelled UV.
